main_body: Flat ground patch of beige/pink brick-style paving, with a few blue-grey slate tiles and dark/grey strips at the edges. It is a terrain surface, not a standing object.
top_band: none; terrain tile seen from above, no standing volume
evidence: Terrain kind: a floor/paving patch is a flat ground surface, so the 3/4 top-and-front contract does not apply. The brick pattern is a surface texture with no standing volume, no side faces and no front elevation. Judged as a terrain tile, it passes.

style.evidence: The candidate is a repeating brick/paving pattern in beige, pink-beige and grey-brown with dark grey mortar. Mortar lines are a tinted dark grey, not pure black. It has about 4 lightness steps (light beige, mid beige, pink-brown, dark grey mortar), against about 5-6 in the paving reference, which has stones shaded one by one with light edge highlights. Many bricks are flat 5x3 or larger beige blocks with little grain or per-brick variation, so large areas are flat fills. The repeating pattern also looks mechanical. Blue-grey and dark-green strips are single-tone blocks with only a few accent pixels. Tile density is lower than the reference's information-rich tiles, so it falls short of the Beodeul standard.
